transcript:
>> This is NPR News Now.
The latest headlines every hour.
>> Live from NPR News, I'm Giles Snyder.
House Republicans have scuttled an impeachment effort targeting Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth.
The vote to effectively block impeachment charges from being considered past 211 to
204.
Here's NPR's Eric McDaniel.
>> Kentucky Republican Representative Thomas Massie spearheaded this impeachment effort
on his way out of Congress.
And the charges he filed were tied to failure to get congressional approval for military
action in Iran and Yemen, as well as strikes against what the administration says are drugboats
in the Caribbean and Pacific, and a Pentagon effort to publish a Democratic Senator, Mark
Kelly of Arizona, who told service members not to follow illegal orders.
Hegseth called the charges a sham, and the White House backed him up.
Most Republicans, even those openly critical of the administration's relationship with
Congress in terms of war powers, agree.
The impeachment effort is now dead.
Eric McDaniel, NPR News, Capitol Hill.
>> Vote counting ongoing and outstanding Senate races in Alaska and Mississippi, where Democrat
Scott Colom holds a narrow lead over Republican incumbent Cindy Hyde Smith.
Colom was optimistic when he spoke to reporters in Jackson Tuesday.
>> I'm very confident based on the performance of the ballots in Hides County on election
day, once these affidavit ballots come in from Hides County, then the lead is gonna
be insurmountable.
>> In Alaska, Democrat Mary Peltola increased her lead Tuesday, Alaska Public Media reporting
that election officials have counted more than 24,000 additional votes, and Peltola
leads Republican incumbent Dan Sullivan 49% to 47%.
Capitol Hill lawmakers renewing calls for tighter restrictions on China's access to
advanced artificial intelligence chips.
Senate Democratic leader Chuck Schumer wants Congress to take action after allegations
that Nvidia CEO Jensen Hwang was the target of an alleged Chinese spy.
US and UK counterintelligence officials say an American soldier has been arrested, and
Piers Quill Lawrence reports a 41-year-old man is suspected of spying for Russia.
>> UK Metropolitan Police said the man was arrested near Gloucester in the southwest
of England, and that searches were being carried out at two locations there.
US Army Counterintelligence Command described the suspect as a senior soldier entrusted
with sensitive information.
In a statement released by the UK, FBI Director Kash Patel praised the partnership of the
two countries.
In recent weeks, US bases in the UK have been on high alert for possible attacks linked
to the war in Iran.
The UK statement said this latest arrest was not linked to any other ongoing investigations.
Quill Lawrence, NPR News.
>> Several members of the Kennedy family are joining efforts aimed at stopping President
Trump from building his proposed triumphal arch in Washington, DC.
They filed documents Tuesday to join a court case against the arch construction.
It's currently on hold.
A judge issued a temporary order blocking it through November 19th.
This is NPR.
The Ebola outbreak in Democratic Republic of Congo now tops 11,000.
Government figures show confirmed infections total 11,042, and that more than 5,300 people
have died.
Health officials say the outbreak is being driven by a rare strain of the Ebola virus
for which there are no approved treatments or vaccines.
In Gaza, a grandmother survived a deadly landslide that buried several tents sheltering displaced
families during recent heavy rain in Piers-on-Nasbaba rewards.
>> 58-year-old Umel Abid Al-Sahar was sleeping in her tent when the rain started.
Within minutes, the sand cliff above her collapsed, burying her and her daughter up to their waist.
This survived, but the neighboring tents were completely swallowed by the mud.
From beneath the dirt, she screams for rescuers to save the family in its door.
Abu Salah, whose wife and children were among those buried.
Sahar says displaced families knew the cliffside wasn't safe, but had nowhere else to pitch
their tents.
She says people throw themselves under mountains into the sea, anywhere they can find a place
to shelter.
Tell us where should we go?
>> Anas Babur, NPR News, Gaza.
>> The financial markets in Asia, largely advancing in Wednesday trading, shares in
Taiwan leading the way, more than 3% after a sharp sell-off last week in technology stocks.
Asian markets are up after Wall Street lost ground following the government's latest read
on inflation.
The Labor Department says inflation ran hotter than expected last month.
I'm Jaiel Snyder.
This is NPR News.

topics.text: House Republicans scuttle impeachment effort against Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth, 211 to 204
Vote counting continues in Mississippi Senate race, Democrat Scott Colom narrowly leads Cindy Hyde Smith
Democrat Mary Peltola extends lead over Republican Dan Sullivan in Alaska Senate race
Congressional Democrats push tighter limits on China's access to advanced AI chips after alleged spy report
Army soldier arrested in UK on suspicion of spying for Russia near Gloucester
Kennedy family joins lawsuit against Trump's proposed triumphal arch in Washington, DC
Ebola outbreak in Democratic Republic of Congo tops 11,000 infections, over 5,300 deaths
Gaza grandmother survives landslide that buried displaced families' tents in Deir al-Balah
Asian stock markets advance Wednesday, Taiwan shares up over 3%, after hotter inflation report
